key_insight: Distributed quantum-centric supercomputing combines molecular fragmentation with multi-layered generative learning to reduce quantum and classical computational demands while recovering intermolecular interactions.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets larger electronic-structure calculations by distributing smaller quantum workloads and reconstructing the global solution on classical HPC resources.
method: Solve molecular fragments in parallel using physics-informed generative sample-based quantum diagonalization (PIGen-SQD).
Optimize local-to-global bit assignments to construct a mapped tensor product state.
Use a secondary generative module to identify dominant global configurations and recover inter-fragment correlations.
evidence_signal: Water and formamide dimers showed up to 95% smaller diagonalization dimensions and an order-of-magnitude improvement in energy accuracy over conventional SQD; a 120-qubit water-hexamer problem was split into six 20-qubit subsystems, with dimeric stitching agreeing well with classical references.
watch_item: Accuracy beyond the tested systems remains uncertain, particularly when higher-order inter-fragment correlations exceed the dimeric approximation.
paper_title: Distributed Quantum-Centric Supercomputing with Multi-Layered Generative Learning for Intermolecular Interactions
